name: Gaia × Kenshi Co-Processor Architecture
principle: Kenshi runs CPU-bound on Ogre3D. Gaia claims the idle GPU. Both share the 9950X3D.

cpu.gaia_uses: Remaining 30 threads for mesh processing, mod forge, AI orchestration
cpu.constraint: Kenshi pins one core hard — 3D V-Cache helps with game state cache hits

ram.gaia_uses: All 9.3GB Kenshi data cached + 80GB free for processing

gpu_rtx5090.kenshi_uses: ~5% — Ogre3D draws scene, basic shading, no RT, no compute

gaia_uses.cuda: Mesh processing, vertex transforms, collision detection, batch mod compilation
gaia_uses.rt_cores: Ray casting for occlusion testing, shadow baking, hidden geometry detection
gaia_uses.tensor_cores: AI inference for mod generation, texture super-resolution, NPC behavior prediction
gaia_uses.vram: Full 9.3GB game data + 22GB free for compute buffers and inference models

gpu_rtx5090.headroom: ~95% of all silicon available to Gaia during gameplay

gpu_igpu.note: Frees RTX from display duty — pure compute subsystem

background.gpu_usage: CUDA compute + RT cores + Tensor cores
background.priority: BELOW_NORMAL — yields to Kenshi when needed
modes: ANALYZE: Real-time mesh analysis, finding hidden geometry via RT ray casting
FORGE: Batch .mod creation using vertex/material data from analyzed meshes
SHADOW: RT core shadow baking for all loaded zones
PREDICT: Tensor core NPC behavior forecasting
RENDER: Side-by-side KenshiReborn preview window showing enhanced view

live_modding_pipeline.step_1: Kenshi loads zone → Gaia intercepts file reads (mesh, texture, zone)
live_modding_pipeline.step_2: RT cores ray-cast through mesh to find: occluded faces, shadow casters, collision gaps
live_modding_pipeline.step_3: CUDA cores recompute: optimized LODs, merged meshes, better normals
live_modding_pipeline.step_4: Tensor cores infer: texture upscaling, NPC pathing, weather transitions
live_modding_pipeline.step_5: kenshi-mod-forge writes .mod overlay → Kenshi's next load uses improved data
live_modding_pipeline.step_6: Live redox cycle: load → analyze → improve → save → reload
live_modding_pipeline.latency: Single vertex: 0.612μs. Full zone (100K tris): ~60ms. Real-time viable.

steam_workshop_pipeline.create: FCS (Forgotten Construction Set) or kenshi-mod-forge (Rust, automated)
steam_workshop_pipeline.deploy_workshop: SteamCMD or FCS built-in upload → steamcommunity.com/app/233860/workshop/
steam_workshop_pipeline.deploy_nexus: Nexus Mods API (key wired, 1749 existing mods cataloged)

cuda_21760_cores.mesh_merging: Combine submeshes for draw call reduction
cuda_21760_cores.physics_sim: Soft body, cloth, destruction — things Ogre can't do

rt_170_cores.occlusion_culling: Cast rays from camera → mark invisible triangles → skip in next frame
rt_170_cores.shadow_mapping: Pre-bake shadow maps for entire world at startup
rt_170_cores.collision_volumes: Generate precise collision from mesh geometry via ray sweeps
rt_170_cores.hidden_geometry_scan: Find meshes buried underground or inside other meshes

tensor_680_cores.texture_upscale: DLSS-style 2x on all Kenshi textures (2,626 DDS files)
tensor_680_cores.npc_behavior: Train behavior prediction model from 255hrs of play data
tensor_680_cores.mod_recommendation: Suggest compatible mods from Workshop based on play style
tensor_680_cores.speech_synthesis: Voice lines for Dialogue Expansion mods

the_pitch.message: We rebuilt your renderer in Rust. It loads your meshes. It renders your bull. It runs at 0.6μs/vertex on Vulkan. Here's the Kenshi 2 engine you need — sovereign, no Unreal royalties, no Epic dependency. Just Rust + WGPU + your art.
the_pitch.proof: KenshiReborn v0.4.0 — Kenshi bull rendered on RTX 5090, orbiting camera, three-light rig, Vulkan backend, 22K vertices at 60+ FPS
the_pitch.workshop_presence: Published mods on Workshop demonstrating we can read+write the format
